newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities ended higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities ended higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended slightly higher across the board on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Bond prices ended slightly higher across the board but treasury bill yields ended lower. The interbank rate eased slightly. Volume was only moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.85/1.80 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.03/1.98 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.00/1.95 percent against 2.25/2.20 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.43/98.48 from Tuesday's close of S$98.27/98.32, September 2001 at S$97.15/97.20 versus S$97.00/97.05 and June 2003 at S$95.15/95.20 against S$94.85/94.90.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent from Tuesday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
